evidence.detail: Rows ac1/inside-a-recorded-worktree (a container whose compose working folder label is inside the recorded worktree wt-b, a container on the second context whose second configuration file is, a container with no label and a bind mount whose host source is, and a volume and a network that carry the labels: each has wt-b's owner as proposed owner, with the worktree, the label or mount that gave it and the path in the report; the container and the volume whose label names a same-named folder wt-b outside every worktree, the same pair for wt-a of the act-mode project, and a container in a folder whose name only begins with the worktree's name, have no owner, no proposed owner and no parent), ac1/by-where-the-path-leads (a path that leads into the worktree through a link outside it places the container; a path written inside the worktree that leads out through a link places nothing; the reconciler's worktree_inside answers the same when asked itself), ac1/no-proposal-when-undecided (a path with a .. segment although a bind source is inside, a configuration file that is not an absolute path, paths into two recorded worktrees, a worktree marked gone and a volume shown without its CreatedAt: each is a report with no proposed owner that says why; without the reconciler the adapter reports and proposes nothing, and with it the same record shows the proposed owner), ac1/a-run-label-comes-first (a container with a known run's label is that run's item although it binds a folder of the worktree; one whose label names no known run is a report with no proposal although compose ran inside the worktree). Green: proof/VELDO-0307/suite-green.txt.

The rows run the adapter and the reconciler against a real Ledger on a real control store under one temporary folder, with the installation and two projects read by the real declarations reader; orchard is in act mode by the owner's own signed command with a real key, meadow in report mode. The worktrees are recorded worktree items whose folders are on disk, and the links of the link rows are real links. The tickets end through the real Signal, kind registry, probes, safety rules and removers (loss/nothing-of-theirs-touched). The engine is a stand-in (assumption 1). What compose and the engines really write was measured on both engines of the host: proof/VELDO-0307/compose-labels.json.

Further cases, each red on its row: space307-labelled-path-not-protected, space307-compose-project-not-protected, space307-image-known-by-its-tag-alone, space307-covered-report-stays. proof/VELDO-0307/mutations.txt.

The fix of the two protect-list defects. Row protect/image-pattern-every-tag: the patterns minio/minio and minio/mc, which name no tag and no digest, cover that repository's :latest, another tag, a digest and the repository with no tag, on both contexts: the Ledger's declare, adopt and report each refuse it as space_protected:image:<pattern> with nothing written, and rule 2 at removal (control_space_probe.protected) names the same entry; a repository whose name only begins the same, another repository of the same owner and the same repository on another registry are not covered; a pattern that names a tag covers that tag and neither another tag, a digest nor the bare repository; a volume and a container are matched by the name in full as before. Row protect/covered-after-adoption: in the act-mode project three containers (by compose working folder, by the second configuration file, by bind source), a volume and a network are adopted to a recorded worktree while nothing covers them, and rule 2 passes each; the three folders are then added to the protect list; rule 2 refuses each removal as space_deferred:protected with the entry and the path its labels or its mount name now; at the ticket's end through the real Signal and removers none of the five is named to a stop or a remove, each is there (the containers running, the volume with its data) and its item is deferred as protected, while the container nothing covers is stopped and removed, which shows the removal is live; labels the engine does not show at rule 2 refuse the removal (labels_unread).

Ten cases for the two rows, each noop green then mutant red on its row. protect/image-pattern-every-tag: space307-ledger-image-pattern-by-the-full-tag (the defect as it was: the Ledger matches the tag in full), space307-ledger-digest-read-as-a-tag, space307-ledger-tagged-pattern-covers-every-tag, space307-rule-2-image-pattern-by-the-full-tag, space307-rule-2-tagged-pattern-covers-every-tag. protect/covered-after-adoption: space307-rule-2-reads-no-labelled-path (the defect as it was: rule 2 does not read a labelled path), space307-rule-2-unread-labels-pass, space307-rule-2-labelled-paths-not-read, space307-rule-2-configuration-files-not-split, space307-rule-2-labelled-path-beneath-only. proof/VELDO-0307/mutations.txt.

assumptions: 1. THE ENGINE OF THE ROWS IS A STAND-IN, a class in the suite that holds containers, networks, volumes and images for two contexts and refuses as an engine does without a force option. No row asks a real engine. That its records have the shape of a real engine's (the two compose labels on a container as absolute paths, a bind mount as Type bind with a host Source, an image's RepoTags, RepoDigests and Config.Labels) rests on the measurement in compose-labels.json for the container, and for an image on the engine's documented inspect record, which was not measured in this build.

2. ON THE MEASURED ENGINES A NETWORK AND A VOLUME CARRY NEITHER LABEL, so this rule gives them no proposal there. The rows for a volume and a network with the labels prove the code path for an engine that writes them; no such engine was seen.

3. NOTHING SETS Service.space_docker YET, as in VELDO-0306, so no adapter runs in a service and nothing passes it the reconciler in production. Without the reconciler the adapter behaves as VELDO-0306 left it, apart from the protect check coming first.

4. RULE 2 AT REMOVAL NOW READS A LABELLED PATH (fixed after the build, by the lead's instruction; the footprint is extended in the spec's History). It reads the object's labels from the engine again at every judged removal, one more inspect per Docker item, and refuses when they cannot be read. A bind source is read as before by control_space_probe.mounts. Act mode is refused until VELDO-0332 and 0339.
5. A BIND SOURCE IS READ AS A PATH OF THIS HOST. An engine context that reaches an engine on another host would report that host's paths; the installation's two contexts are local sockets.

6. ONE EARLIER CASE MOVED WITH THE CODE: space306-compose-project-not-in-the-locator now carries a second edit, because the adapter reads the compose project label against the protect list itself before the ledger does, and the defect needs both readings gone. With both, its row ac1/protected is red as before.

7. AN IMAGE NAME IS READ AS WRITTEN. The Ledger and rule 2 take the repository as the name without its tag (what follows the last colon when no / comes after it) and without its digest (what follows @). A registry host or the library/ prefix an engine may leave out or add is not made the same: minio/minio does not cover registry.example:5000/minio/minio. The adapter's listing of protected images (image_names) is unchanged: it knows an image by each tag in full and by each repository, so a pattern that names a digest is matched by the Ledger and rule 2 and not by that listing.
rollback: Revert the change. Objects without a run label stay reports with no proposed owner.
